relations.justification: Engineering derives from classical mechanics; statics and dynamics are its oldest content.
Physiology is the function of structures anatomy describes; the pairing is the oldest ordering in medical education.
Pathology is physiology gone wrong and cannot be read without the normal case.
Pharmacology acts on physiological systems, and dose-response is meaningless without them.
Clinical medicine reasons from signs to mechanism; the mechanism is pathology.
Pharmacology depends on medicinal chemistry for the molecules whose action it studies.
Surgical decision-making is clinical decision-making with an additional instrument.
Psychiatry depends on clinical psychology for its assessment instruments and much of its therapeutic repertoire.
Trauma care in a survival setting is emergency medicine without its infrastructure, and the triage logic is inherited.
Population-level prevention generalises the individual preventive encounter.
Preventive medicine and development economics meet on the same interventions; the cost-effectiveness argument is shared.
A study design is chosen to estimate a frequency measure; the measures are prior to the designs that estimate them.
Bias and confounding are properties of a design; the taxonomy of designs comes first.
Cohort and case-control designs are what established the chronic-disease risk factors; the association claims rest on them.
Comparative epidemiological design and comparative social method share an origin in the problem of causal claims without experiment.
Chronic-disease risk-factor claims are the hardest confounding problem in the field and presuppose its machinery.
Infectious disease epidemiology depends on the contact-network structure that determines whether transmission takes hold.
Epidemic spread is the canonical example of diffusion on a network and the source of most of its vocabulary.
Epidemiological findings on chronic disease support the human-capital account of why health investment has economic returns.
Health-system design requires evaluation evidence; without it financing choices are made on assertion.
A screening programme requires a measured disease frequency: the positive predictive value of any test depends on prevalence, so screening a rare condition harms more than it helps.
Modern epidemiological method and survey methodology developed together and share their sampling theory.
Public health claims are statistical claims; the discipline is inseparable from its inferential machinery.
Exercise physiology is systems physiology under load.
Training theory is the applied form of the adaptation physiology describes.
Biomechanics and structural mechanics are one analysis; the body is a linkage of levers under load.
Injury mechanism is a biomechanical account; prevention follows from the loading analysis.
Motor learning and domain pedagogy are the same problem of skill acquisition approached from movement and from instruction.
A training programme requires the adaptation physiology it is trying to provoke; periodisation without the physiological rationale is arbitrary.
Sports medicine is clinical medicine specialised to the musculoskeletal consequences of training.
Sports science is applied systems physiology; the exercise case is physiology under a controlled perturbation.
Veterinary science is medicine whose patients are other species; the physiology is comparative, not different in kind.
Production medicine derives from animal husbandry and retains its economic frame.
Building structures is structural engineering applied to occupied space.
Building physics performance claims require stated measurement uncertainty; an envelope figure without one cannot be verified on site.
Urban planning depends on administrative law for the instruments — zoning, permitting, compulsory purchase — that make a plan operative.
Manufacturing derives from mechanical engineering and adds the economics of repetition.
Transportation engineering derives from civil and mechanical engineering with a network overlay.
Energy engineering derives from thermodynamics; conversion efficiency is a second-law statement.
Grid operation exemplifies resilience engineering: reserve margin is bought robustness and its cost is explicit.
Modulation and multiplexing specialise channel coding to a physical medium.
Telecommunications network architecture and computer networking are one layered model approached from two histories.
Spectrum management depends on competition principles when allocating a scarce resource among rivals.
Genetic engineering is molecular biology made directional; the techniques are the mechanisms.
Genetic engineering requires containment as a constituent practice, not an afterthought — the products reproduce themselves.
Industrial biotechnology requires manufacturing engineering to scale; the flask-to-reactor transition is a process-engineering problem, not a biological one.
Medical biotechnology is medicine practised with engineered biological agents.
Bioinformatics specialises algorithm design to sequence and structure data.
Bioinformatics emerged from computer science applied to sequence data.
Nanoscale behaviour is quantum confinement and surface energetics — the departures from bulk are physical results.
The nanoscale regime is what gives nanomaterials properties their bulk counterparts lack; the size is the cause, not a correlate.
Nanoscale application requires the safety assessment, because the property that makes the material useful is the one that makes it mobile in tissue.
The toxicological concern is caused by the scale itself: particles small enough to cross biological barriers do so because of the surface-to-volume regime.
